correctness.rationale: For 0<q<1 and r>0, S_{q,r} has a unit principal residue at t=1, theta multiplier −r^(−1), and exactly the pole lattice q^(2Z). For odd L, S^L and all Euler derivatives of S_{q,r^L} share multiplier −r^(−L). The L-dimensional principal parts D^j(1−t)^(−1) are triangular with diagonal j!, so a unique polynomial P of degree L−1 cancels all pole parts. The difference is globally holomorphic on C* and has multiplier −r^(−L). Its global Laurent coefficients satisfy (q^(2n)+r^(−L))b_n=0 and vanish. The original positive Laurent product proves P(n)>0 for every integer. For r=q, direct principal-part calculation gives P_3(n)=(n+1)(n+2)/2+3E(q). An exponentially dominated midpoint Riemann sum gives E(e^(−h))~π²/(24h²). The actual bundled checker passed 123 identity/cubic comparisons plus additional positivity/leading-term checks. Numerical checks supplement rather than prove the arbitrary-parameter identity.

value.rationale: The exact cubic coefficient sequence addresses the explicitly described unresolved higher-power Gaussian Laurent realization in Katori–Shirai and enables immediate independent-Gaussian simulation without infinite convolutions. The full odd hierarchy reduces each higher kernel power to finitely many Euler derivatives of a single weighted Szegő kernel, with a constructive degree bound, strict coefficient positivity, and a new thin-annulus correction law. These are natural structural and computational facts about canonical analytic covariance kernels, not an arbitrary finite slice or known coefficient table.
